per_finding.notes: Basename allowlist works. REVF-H4a-r3-probe/scripts/stamp.sh: orchestrator-directive.json, Orchestrator-Directive.json, planning-edit-override, roadmap-edit-override, mode, skill-invocations, trivial/Trivial/TRIVIAL, STATE/state, branch, 'trivial ', 'trivial.', 'x-usage.', 'x-usage ', trailing '/', './', 'sub/..', '..', trivial/../x-usage, unicode look-alikes (x-uságe, fullwidth x, zero-width space), '-usage', absolute /etc and outside-dir paths, and a symlinked dir all fall back to graphify-query. The directive stays {"next_skill":"silver-plan","blocking":true}. Names that match the pattern are honoured, as designed: skill-invocations-usage, trivial-usage, TRIVIAL-USAGE, agentmemory-usage (no SB control file ends in -usage or -query). But the PARENT components are never checked against SB control names, and sb_rt_stamp_write runs mkdir -p on the parent, so a stamp can turn a control path into a directory. See major issue 1.

REVF-H4a-r3-probe/scripts/lock.sh: 8 rounds, each with a stale (dead-pid) lock, then 7 parallel grants and 7 parallel revokes. Every round: granted=7, after_revoke=0, and no lock, takeover or tmp files left. A pid-less lock is reclaimed after the wait: rc 0, grant recorded, about 1.5 s with TRIES=5. A live owner gives rc 2 and keeps the lock. Non-numeric, zero, negative and empty SB_CONSENT_LOCK_TRIES fall back to 100. Residuals are in minor issue 3.

REVF-H4a-r3-probe/scripts/fp.sh, 152 commands x 5 gates, Claude Bash; 28 commands under Codex exec_command. Denied in all 5 gates: git --no-pager commit, git -c alias.ci=commit ci, git $'commit', merge/cherry-pick/revert/am/commit-tree/rebase, git --work-tree/-C/-c commit, xargs/find -exec/eval/bash -c, npm -g install, pnpm/bun add -g, yarn global add, | /bin/bash, | env bash, | python3, | sudo bash, bash <(curl), python3 <(curl), sh -c "$(curl)", pipx/cargo/go/gem/uv tool install, brew install, writes. Allowed in all 5: $PYTHON -m pytest, "$PY" -m pytest, pytest, make, make -j4, cargo build/test, go test/build/vet, gradle/gradlew, docker ps/build/compose, kubectl get, terraform plan, npm test/ci/install/run, pip install -r, uv run, uvx, npx, mvn, git status/log/diff/push. kubectl apply and terraform apply are now gated: F2 classifies them as deploys, which is consistent with the delivery tier. Remaining allows are outside the r2 examples: a repo-config alias (git ci), npm --location=global, brew reinstall, pip install --user, and analyzer-missed writes (patch, git apply, python3 script.py).

One scoped run: 127 test files, including test-gate-hooks-fault-injection.sh and every test that references a changed gate or lib, with --only over all 30 changed hooks/ and scripts/ files. issues.location: hooks/lib/recommended-tools.sh:207-213 (sb_rt_state_file) with :236 (sb_rt_stamp_write mkdir -p); tests/hooks/test-graphify-gate-lib-coverage.sh 'state path in a not-yet-existing subdirectory is accepted'; docs/CONSENT.md:27
issues.problem: The allowlist checks only the basename. A configured stamp ${SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR}/<control-name>/x-usage is honoured, and the stamp writer's mkdir -p creates a DIRECTORY named after an SB control file. With orchestrator-directive.json made a directory, sb_orchestrator_directive_write returns 0 but writes orchestrator-directive.json/orchestrator-directive.json.tmp inside it, and sb_orchestrator_directive_is_blocking stays false for good. This is the same blocking-directive bypass as the r2 major, reached by one more path component, and it persists. state/x-usage makes the skill state file a directory: commits stay denied (fail closed), but honest skill recording breaks. docs/CONSENT.md says such a stamp 'can never name one of SB's own state files'.
issues.evidence: REVF-H4a-r3-probe/scripts/stamp.sh (graphify enforce consent, record-graphify-query.sh on 'graphify query x'): '${SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR}/orchestrator-directive.json/x-usage' -> ./orchestrator-directive.json ./orchestrator-directive.json/x-usage; the same for state/, trivial/, planning-edit-override/, roadmap-edit-override/, mode/, branch/. Then, with SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR holding a directory orchestrator-directive.json: source hooks/lib/orchestrator-directive.sh; sb_orchestrator_directive_write silver-plan '' r true -> write_rc=0, then is_blocking -> not-blocking; the file lands at orchestrator-directive.json/orchestrator-directive.json.tmp. Separately, dev-cycle-check.sh does not deny 'echo 1 > ~/.claude/.silver-bullet/orchestrator-directive.json', which is pre-existing and outside this package.
issues.suggested_fix: Require rel to be a single component (reject any '/' in rel), or put custom stamps under a dedicated $SB_RUNTIME_STATE_DIR/opt-in/ subdirectory. Replace the 'subdirectory is accepted' test with a rejection test for orchestrator-directive.json/x-usage and state/x-usage, and assert that no directory is created.

issues.location: hooks/lib/user-consent.sh:161-200; tests/hooks/test-user-consent.sh 'SB_CONSENT_LOCK_TRIES=... falls back to the default'
issues.problem: (a) The bad-TRIES tests are vacuous: no lock is held, so the loop body never runs. With the validation line removed (mutation in a copy), test-user-consent.sh still passes 141/0. (b) A leftover <lock>.takeover directory (process killed inside _sb_consent_lock_reclaim) disables every future stale-lock takeover, and the error message names only <lock>; one test pins the status-2 behaviour. (c) A huge TRIES value such as 99999999999999999999 matches the regex, so a held lock is waited on practically forever (the probe hung and was killed).
issues.evidence: mutation: sed '176s/.*/  :/' hooks/lib/user-consent.sh in REVF-H4a-r3-probe/mut -> test-user-consent.sh Results: 141 passed, 0 failed. lock.sh: stale lock plus stale .takeover -> rc 2 after 10.6 s.
issues.suggested_fix: Test bad TRIES with an ownerless lock held, and assert rc 0 within the default wait. Treat a .takeover directory older than a few seconds as stale, or name it in the message. Cap TRIES at, for example, 1000.
